messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: hosted-runtime-1 reported repeated KV cache OOMs (kvcache/oom). 23 model-runner hosts affected, elevated 5xx rate for text-generation. Auto-escalating to on-call.

Alex: noticing huge increase in kvcache memory due to extremely long prompts getting prefetched into sessions. These sessions keep their KV windows pinned because continuous-batching backlog never drains.

Maya: confirmation — I can reproduce locally with a 180k token prompt + recent batching/heuristic flag. Prefetch heuristics are pre-loading entire context if prefix similarity > 0.7. That combined with increased max_batch_window_ms is bad.

Jordan: fyi I pushed the batching heuristics change in commit abc123def yesterday to reduce empty batches but I didn't account for very long-context tails. Rolling that back now if needed.

Sam: I’m on pager, taking lead. First mitigation: throttle prefetch and cap session KV length. Can someone run the feature-flag toggle and set session cap? @Jordan @Maya

OpsBot: Running command to set feature flag...
```
# toggle prefetch for hosted runtime
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/flags/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"hosted_prefetch_enabled","value":false}'
```

OpsBot: Feature flag update queued; patch applied to control plane, rolling to region us-west1.

Alex: pushing an immediate session cap via runtime config: set `max_kvcache_tokens_per_session=30000` while we triage. This will evict extreme long sessions.

Maya: applying runtime patch now on the control plane:
```
kubectl patch configmap runtime-config -n hosted \
  --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_kvcache_tokens_per_session":"30000"}}'
```

OpsBot: Patch applied to control plane; worker pods will reload config on next restart. For immediate effect we can recycle runners with the highest mem usage.

Jordan: rolling back batching change (abc123def -> restore commit zyx987). Rolling restart beginning; will replace 5 runners at a time to avoid disruption.

Support: initial customer impact check — approximate 0.8% of active hosted customers saw increased error rate (5xx) between 14:02–14:12 UTC. A few premium customers reported failed requests and elevated latency.

Sam: drafting status update for status.redwood.ai: short note saying we’re mitigating a prefetch/cache regression causing intermittent failures and elevated latency; will update in 30m. @Support please review.

Support: drafted. Suggest calling out affected region (us-west1) and that we’ve applied throttle + session caps; no customer data exposure.

Alex: additionally enabling aggressive eviction for prefetched keys: set `kvcache.prefetch_eviction_policy=LRU_AGGRESSIVE` for hosted runtime.

Maya: done. Also toggled `continuous_batching.max_window_ms` back to 200 (was 1200). That should reduce backlog retention.

OpsBot: Observability: 90th/99th percentile memory on runner hosts dropping after restart, errors trending down.

Jordan: rollback of batching change completed, no config drift. Monitoring for regressions.

Sam: ok initial mitigations complete. Next steps: longer-term fix will be to implement prompt-length gating in prefetch heuristic and add soft-kick for oversized prefixes before prefetching. Jordan will own the code fix.

Jordan: will file a PR with gating and a unit test for long prompt cases, targeting patch release tomorrow EOD.

Alex: for immediate follow-up, recommend a canary that rejects prefetch for sessions > 25k tokens, and add metric `kvcache.prefetch_skipped_due_to_length`.

Support: preparing customer outbound for impacted customers (email template + support replies) — ready to send once we have final error window and mitigation summary.

Sam: handing off active follow-up to Jordan (next 4 hours). If error rate spikes again, I’ll re-escalate and take the pager back. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Jordan: acknowledged — will finish PR, add dashboard for `prefetch_skipped_due_to_length`, and coordinate a postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident resolved for now — error rate back to baseline. Recording incident tag: kvcache-prefetch-flood. Pager closed.

Support: final note — estimated customer impact window 14:02–14:12 UTC, ~0.8% customers, majority recovered within 5 minutes after mitigations.

Sam: final handoff: Jordan owns follow-ups; Alex to validate regression tests; Maya to validate observability flags. Leaving note in #incidents-runbook.

Jordan: will publish postmortem draft in 24 hours.
